page: Microsoft Azure E32ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU includes 48 MB of Level 3 cache and supports AVX-512 vector extensions, AES cryptography acceleration, and bit manipulation instructions. The system features 256 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8 GB of memory allocated per virtual core.

Storage consists of 1288 GB of local SSD capacity alongside support for Azure Premium Storage, with zero bundled GPUs. In synthetic and application-level testing, the instance exhibits consistent mid-tier performance across multi-core compute and data processing suites. The PassMark CPU test recorded 36,757.75 points, while multi-core stress-ng reached 31,080.73. Memory throughput tests demonstrated 143.87 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 67.31 GB/sec for writes. In-memory operations scored 31.13 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks, and database operations achieved 15,337.83 points in PassMark.

The 1:8 core-to-memory allocation makes the E32ds_v5 cost-effective for memory-constrained workloads where compute scaling is secondary. However, the absence of hardware accelerators limits efficiency for large-scale machine learning, as evidenced by large 70B parameter LLM prompt processing executing at 6.67 tokens per second. The server is well suited for enterprise relational databases, large in-memory caches, data analytics pipelines, and memory-intensive ETL tasks needing high RAM density and fast local scratch storage.
description: Microsoft Azure E32ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor with 32 dedicated vCPUs, 16 physical cores, and 48 MB of L3 cache. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the configuration provides 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside 1288 GB of local SSD scratch storage and zero discrete GPUs. Benchmark results position the server solidly in middle-tier enterprise performance, producing 36,757.75 points in PassMark CPU, 31.13 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations, and 143.87 GB/sec in large uncached memory reads. While lack of hardware acceleration constrains large LLM throughput, the substantial memory footprint and local disk allocation offer reliable resource density. The E32ds_v5 is best suited for production relational databases, Redis or Memcached clusters, in-memory data processing, and enterprise ETL pipelines.
